correctness.rationale: Each single-stage T_w fixes its perpendicular neutral vector e_w and has squared singular matrix kI+δ e_w e_w^T, where δ=h²(1−h²), k=1−δ. The product P=T_v T_u gives P^TP=k²I+kδ aa^T+δbb^T with a=e_u and b=T_u^T e_v; its rank-two Gram matrix has trace δ(2k+δc²), determinant δ²k²(1−c²), yielding the three claimed singular values for 0≤h≤1. Independently recomputed exact symbolic characteristic polynomial for rational unit overlap (c,s)=(3/5,4/5), h=1/2. The derivative sign identity (2−δc²)²−c²(4(1−δ)+δ²c²)=4(1−c²)>0 gives unique δ=1/4 at h²=1/2 for c<1. At h>1 each stage σ_min=1 and hence P has σ_min≥1, excluding a better global step; c=1 neutral direction gives norm1. Angular derivative at c=1 is 1/7, giving θ²/14. No Floquet spectral-radius optimality is inferred.

value.rationale: The sharp worst-case one-period contraction factor and universal step are motivated numerical-optimization invariants for a natural minimal noncommuting time-periodic game. The exact angle-dependent defect quantifies loss near common null directions and provides an actionable deterministic tuning principle, while carefully not claiming runtime or asymptotic spectral radius optimization.

final_claim: For two alternating unit 1×2 real bilinear payoff rows and equal-step extragradient, the entire period singular spectrum depends only on c=|u·v|, and for c<1 the unique operator-norm-minimizing real h≥0 is 1/√2 with exact minimum (sqrt(48+c²)+c)/8 and near-parallel defect θ²/14.
limitations: Only equal-step, two-stage 1x2 real unit payoff vectors; no claims about higher-dimensional neutral coordinates.
Optimizes a one-period Euclidean operator norm, not Floquet asymptotic rate, arbitrary stochastic dynamics, or runtime.
Only one rational symbolic specialization independently rerun; analytic rank-two derivation supplies generality.
